items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Like Arthur Lake, you see. He was another one, you see -- tap dancer, and he became -- he played Dagwood and Harold T., like that, you know.

ctx.x: Initially, though, did she start out as a tap dancer?

No, no. As a champion -- she started out as -- she was developed for championship dancing, you know, and that was a family thing, you see. I think she's an only child, you see. And that's the way it was. I think her father -- he was some kind of producer or something, you know. Very important person at the time. When she was a young one, a little girl, you see. Like Arthur Lake, you see. He was another one, you see -- tap dancer, and he became -- he played Dagwood and Harold T., like that, you know.

Okay, let's move on -- let's move on to the big band era and those different places that you used to perform. Just give me one of the places and tell me about that experience -- the band that you were with, arriving there, what it was like, who was there, what kind of show it was, what was the format of the show, and would you travel by bus to get to a place generally, and when you arrived there where would you stay, was there any discrimination between blacks and whites --
